title.narrative: Karachi Bus Rapid Transit Red Line Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will help increase the use of quality public transport in Karachi by delivering the 26.6-kilometer (km) Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line corridor and associated facilities, directly benefiting 1.5 million people. The project is economically justified by major time savings for BRT passengers; vehicle operating cost savings; and better air quality and reduced carbon emissions through an innovative waste-to-fuel scheme, which will improve the public health and mitigate climate change. It will also make Karachi safer, greener, and more inclusive and competitive.The project is aligned with the following impact: quality of life in Karachi improved. The project will have the following outcome: use of quality public transport in Karachi increased.

Output: BRT operations established Indicator: Modern CNG-hybrid BRT buses (mix of 9-, 12-, or 18-meter lengths) and feeder e-vehicles delivered Progress/Status: Initially planned for modern CNG-hybrid buses and feeder e-vehicles. Updated to modern e-BRT buses (9-, 12- and 18-meters in lengths) only, in line with the government's shift from biomethane to battery-electric buses. Data Source: TransKarachi quarterly project implementation progress reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Output: BRT operations established Indicator: One biogas production plant built and operated through a DBO contract, ensuring at least 80% of the required fuel supply for the fleet Progress/Status: due to the change in propulsion technology from CNG to full-electric, the biogas produced will now be sold to the market and a percentage of the revenue will be given to TKC as non-fare revenue to subsidize the cost of electricity it purchases from the grid, improving the system's financial sustainability. Its CAPEX also significantly increased from USD 10.2 million [initial costing] to USD 27 million [revised costing based on the feasibility study and updated items' rate]. The plant will now be conceived as a commercially viable standalone project financed under a PPP arrangement, through (i) a mix of debt and equity from the private concessionaire/operator; and (ii) a viability gap funding [VGF] up to USD 14 million from the GCF [USD 10.2 million concessional loan + USD 3.8 million grant]. The project is being restructured by TKC with the support of ADB-financed consultants. Data Source: TransKarachi quarterly project implementation progress reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
